Package com.example.inelasticsearch.grpc

Class DataNodeServiceImpl

java.lang.Object
com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DataNodeServiceGrpc.DataNodeServiceImplBase
com.example.inelasticsearch.grpc.DataNodeServiceImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DataNodeServiceGrpc.AsyncService, io.grpc.BindableService, AutoCloseable
public class DataNodeServiceImpl extends com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DataNodeServiceGrpc.DataNodeServiceImplBase implements AutoCloseable
The gRPC DataNodeService implementation that runs on every data node (Server hosts one). This is where documents actually get written to and read from Lucene — everything upstream (Client, CoordinatorServiceImpl) is just routing to reach one of these. One ShardRouter is kept per index name (routersByIndex), lazily created on first use.

Three constructors correspond to three ways this class gets used:

  • DataNodeServiceImpl(Path, int) — single-node mode, owns every shard, no replication. Used by nothing in production but convenient for quick local testing.
  • DataNodeServiceImpl(Path, int, Set) — multi-node mode without topology awareness: owns a fixed shard set, no replication. Mostly a test seam ( DataNodeServiceImplTest) now that the topology-aware constructor below covers real multi-node deployments.
  • DataNodeServiceImpl(Path, ClusterTopology, String) — what Server always uses: stores every shard this node owns as primary or replica, and knows how to push writes out to peers. This is the one with replication and shard-scoped search.

Write path: indexDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexResponse>)/bulkIndexDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.BulkIndexRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.BulkIndexResponse>)/deleteDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DeleteRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DeleteResponse>) are the client-facing RPCs (only ever called for a shard's primary — nothing here enforces that, it's upheld by CoordinatorServiceImpl only routing writes to ClusterTopology.nodeFor(int)). After committing locally, a successful write or delete is asynchronously pushed to that shard's replicas via replicateAsync(java.lang.String, java.util.List<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.Document>)/replicateDeleteAsync(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) using the peer-to-peer replicateDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexResponse>)/replicateBulkIndex(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.BulkIndexRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.BulkIndexResponse>)/replicateDelete(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DeleteRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.DeleteResponse>) RPCs, which apply the change locally and never forward it again (that's what stops replication from looping).

Read path: search(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.SearchRequest, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.SearchResponse>) defaults to this node's primary shards only, so a coordinator fanning a request out to every node never gets the same document back twice from both its primary and a replica copy. The coordinator overrides this by setting shard_ids explicitly on the request — both for replica-fallback when a primary is down, and (see ShardCopySelector) for normal round-robin load-balanced reads.

      public void indexDocument(com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexRequest request, io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver<com.example.inelasticsearch.rpc.IndexResponse> responseObserver)
      Client-facing single-document write. Applies locally, replies immediately, then (if this is topology-aware and this node is the shard's primary) kicks off async replication — the caller never waits on replication completing.
